stem: A 45-year-old man has had four attacks of acute podagra in a year despite avoiding alcohol and red meat. His creatinine is normal. Serum uric acid is 11.4 mg/dL, and a 24-hour urine collection contains 800 mg of uric acid (normal below about 600 mg). He wants a daily drug to prevent attacks.
oneliner: 45M + recurrent podagra + serum urate 11.4 + 24-h urine urate 800 mg + normal creatinine → which prophylactic drug?
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term drug?

whyNot.B: Uricosuric; **adds to the urinary urate load** and risks stones in an overproducer
whyNot.C: Uricosuric with the **same problem** of high urinary urate
whyNot.D: Treats the **acute attack** and prevents flares, but **does not lower urate**

why: **High urinary urate** = **overproducer**. **Allopurinol** blocks **xanthine oxidase** and lowers production; uricosurics suit **underexcretors** only.

drug.name: Allopurinol
drug.how: Blocks conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid
drug.watch: Rash, hepatotoxicity, raises azathioprine and 6-MP levels; do not start during an acute attack

stem: A 54-year-old woman with seropositive, erosive rheumatoid arthritis remains active despite methotrexate and a TNF inhibitor. Her rheumatologist wants to add a drug that depletes B cells.
oneliner: 54F + seropositive erosive RA + active despite methotrexate and a TNF inhibitor + B-cell depletion wanted → which drug?
ask: Which drug is the most appropriate addition?

whyNot.A: CTLA-4-Ig: blocks **B7–CD28 costimulation** of T cells; does not **deplete B cells**
whyNot.B: Blocks the **IL-6 receptor**; does not **deplete B cells**
whyNot.C: **IL-1 receptor antagonist**; does not **deplete B cells**
whyNot.D: Oral **JAK inhibitor** blocking cytokine signalling; does not **deplete B cells**

why: **Rituximab** binds **CD20** on B cells and depletes them; in RA it is given with **methotrexate** after **TNF-inhibitor failure**. The other options also treat refractory RA but act on costimulation, cytokines or JAK signalling.

idea.rule: Anti-CD20 antibody: depletes B cells (not plasma cells, which lack CD20).
also: Used for CD20-positive non-Hodgkin lymphoma and CLL
Used for ITP and other autoimmune cytopenias
Reactivates hepatitis B, so screen first

drug.name: Rituximab
drug.how: Depletes B cells by ADCC, complement lysis and apoptosis
drug.use: Rheumatoid arthritis after TNF inhibitor failure, B-cell lymphoma, CLL, ANCA vasculitis
drug.watch: Infusion reactions, hepatitis B reactivation, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
